title: 2020 ESC Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation

definitions.AF Classification: First detected, paroxysmal, persistent, long-standing persistent, permanent
definitions.CHA2DS2-VASc: CHF(1), HTN(1), Age≥75(2), DM(1), Stroke/TIA(2), Vascular disease(1), Age 65–74(1), Female sex(1)
definitions.Integrated AF Care: ABC pathway: A=Anticoagulation, B=Better symptom management, C=Cardiovascular risk factor control
definitions.EHRA Score: Symptom severity: I (no symptoms) to IVb (disabling symptoms)

recommendations.text: Oral anticoagulation is recommended for all male patients with AF and CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2 and all female patients with CHA2DS2-VASc ≥3.
NOACs (apixaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, rivaroxaban) are recommended in preference to VKA in NOAC-eligible patients with AF.
VKA (warfarin, INR 2–3) remains recommended for AF patients with moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis or mechanical heart valves.
Anticoagulation should not be prescribed to male patients with CHA2DS2-VASc = 0 or female patients with CHA2DS2-VASc = 1.
Rate control is recommended for patients with AF and rapid ventricular rate to improve symptoms.
Lenient rate control (resting HR <110 bpm) is recommended as an initial rate-control target for AF.
Rhythm control (cardioversion, AADs, catheter ablation) is recommended for symptomatic AF to improve quality of life.
Catheter ablation (PVI) is recommended for symptomatic paroxysmal or persistent AF when AADs are ineffective or not tolerated.
Catheter ablation is recommended as first-line rhythm control in selected symptomatic AF patients with HF to improve LVEF.
Management of comorbidities and risk factors (hypertension, obesity, DM, sleep apnoea, alcohol) is recommended as an integral part of AF management.
Screening for AF in patients >65 years with pulse taking or ECG recording is recommended.
Left atrial appendage occlusion may be considered in patients with CI to anticoagulation.

abc_pathway.A: Anticoagulation/Avoid stroke — OAC in patients with risk factors
abc_pathway.B: Better symptom management — rate or rhythm control based on patient preference and symptoms
abc_pathway.C: Cardiovascular risk factors and comorbidity optimisation — hypertension, DM, obesity, sleep apnoea, alcohol, physical activity

pharmacotherapy.examples: apixaban 5 mg BID, rivaroxaban 20 mg OD, dabigatran 150 mg BID, edoxaban 60 mg OD

pharmacotherapy.indication: Rhythm control in structural heart disease
Rhythm control, no HF or severe structural disease
